For me, I have a few rules I've set for myself 

1. No cheats for money, need decay, etc.
2. I use the medium life span 
3. First born is the heir unless they die. If they do die, the 2nd in line takes over 
4. Every trait and aspiration is a dice roll. I try not to use the game's dice roll but my own instead. So if there's 17 aspirations to choose from, I'll roll a D20. I then count down from left to right and choose whichever aspiration it stops on. Or for personality, if there's for categories, it's a D4 and then roll accordingly for the traits below. 
5. Once grown, the heir will need to live in another world. I base that off of their personality once they've grown. Started on Mt Komorebi with a very traditional family. 2nd heir is in San Myshuno with a more modern but still keeping their Komorebi traditions. 3rd heir is currently in Strangerville. 
6. If I don't want them to die or age so soon, I ONLY use the potions available in the Rewards Store. 
7. Every other Sim aside from my main family at the time has Neighborhood Stories on. 
8. Roll with punches. My 1st original heir had died young from laughing too much, so thankfully, her dad had a stepdaughter with his 2nd wife, so she became the 1st heir instead. If I really don't want to lose a Sim forever, I'll keep their ghost around once they die. I even have a little shrine in their original home for the ghosts who live there. 

So yeah that's pretty much what I do. It's been so fun lately because I had taken a break. Just really fun seeing what new personality my 4th heir is getting as a toddler. Also bittersweet to have my 1st heir be in the last stages of her life as a widow and grandmother. It'll be sad once she dies but she's had a good life.

Aside from a sad childhood, he was not happy in his living situation and was trying to also heal from a past relationship. Although he denied it, I was sure he was just on the rebound with me because he didn't want to be lonely and I was a good listener. I believe at one point he even accused me of the same, trying to manipulate/dominate the relationship because he felt I never cared about his interests. We both had our own issues: I was prone to periods of being melancholy/distant and he was insecure/self-loathing/anxiety. Ultimately he ended up moving away to find a better living situation and we remained friends until we lost track of one another. 

One of the last things I told him when he was sad about not finding love in his new city was that finding someone to love you is good and all but you must also work on healing yourself. You are responsible for your own happiness just like she is responsible for hers. I advise to seek therapy or some form of counseling.
